title: Compact self-orthogonal vector bundles give fully faithful derived tensor
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated $A$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $E$ a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module in degree zero (locally a finite rank free module). Put $B=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O_X}(E)$ with composition multiplication. Let $F_E:D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the total derived sheafified tensor $-\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E$ and let $G_E=R\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,-)$ with right $B$-action by precomposition, as constructed in [lem-sfb-bundle-endomorphism-derived-adjunction]. Assume $E$ is compact in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-compact-object], and that for every integer $q\neq0$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,E[q])=0$. Then $F_E$ is fully faithful, and the unit $\operatorname{id}\to G_EF_E$ of that specified adjunction is a natural isomorphism. No generation assumption on $E$ is made.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, dga-lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, degree-zero endomorphism specialization. Its proof uses compactness only on objects in the tensor essential image; by Tag 09M3 these are quasi-coherent, so compactness in D_QCoh suffices.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$ and $\mathcal T=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. The specified adjunction supplies exact functors $F=F_E$, $G=G_E$, $F(B)\simeq E$, and natural identifications $H^qG(K)=\operatorname{Hom}(E,K[q])$ with precomposition action. The categories have all small coproducts: use the module direct-sum statement for $B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the quasi-coherent derived direct-sum statement for $X$. These are coproducts in the same fixed containing universe.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, proof; degree-zero endomorphism case, using its compactness argument only in D_QCoh.

proof.text: For any ring $B$, the regular right module $B_B$ is projective: to lift $f:B\to V$ through a surjection $U\to V$, choose a preimage $u$ of $f(1)$ and use $b\mapsto ub$. The bounded-projective representative theorem therefore computes derived maps from $B[0]$ by chain maps modulo homotopy. A chain map $B[0]\to K[q]$ is exactly a cycle $z=f(1)\in K^q$; the differences of homotopic maps are exactly boundaries (the possible shift sign does not change the boundary subgroup). Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(B,M[q])=H^q(M)$ naturally. This works for noncommutative $B$, using right modules, and for every unbounded $K$.

source.place: Tag 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free, degree-zero ring case; derived passage Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived, equivalently Tag 064B, derived-lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex.

proof.text: The regular object $B$ is compact and weakly generates $\mathcal C$. Indeed the preceding explicit Hom formula identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(B,M[q])$ with $H^q(M)$. Cohomology preserves coproducts (apply the module homology statement to $B^{\mathrm{op}}$), so the canonical compactness map for $B$ is an isomorphism. If every shifted Hom group is zero, the cohomology criterion applied to $0\to M$ makes $M$ zero. This verifies exactly compactness and weak generation, without assuming that $E$ generates $\mathcal T$.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, proof; degree-zero endomorphism case, using its compactness argument only in D_QCoh.

proof.text: The functor $F$ preserves coproducts: for any $N$, adjunction identifies maps $F(\bigoplus_iM_i)\to N$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(FM_i,N)$, with the actual coprojections. For a family $K_i$ in $\mathcal T$, let $c:\bigoplus_iGK_i\to G(\bigoplus_iK_i)$ be induced by $G$ of its coprojections. In degree $q$ its underlying additive map, by the adjunction cohomology formula and module homology of sums, is precisely $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(E,K_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(E,(\bigoplus_iK_i)[q])$. Integer shift is an equivalence and hence preserves coproducts. Compactness of $E$ makes this map bijective. All maps respect the right $B$-actions; a bijective module map has a module-linear inverse. The cohomology criterion therefore makes $c$ an isomorphism. Thus both $F$ and $G$ preserve coproducts.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, proof; degree-zero endomorphism case, using its compactness argument only in D_QCoh.

proof.text: Let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to GF$ be the unit. On $B$ the tensor identification is $B\otimes_B E\to E$, $b\otimes e\mapsto b(e)$. Currying this identity gives $b\mapsto(e\mapsto b(e))$; after a K-injective resolution $j:E\to I$ it is the chain map $B\to\operatorname{Hom}(E,I)$, $b\mapsto j\circ b$. Thus $H^0(\eta_B)$ is the canonical map from ordinary endomorphisms of $E$ to derived endomorphisms, a bijection by full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding. In every other degree its source is zero and its target is $\operatorname{Hom}(E,E[q])=0$ by hypothesis. For $B[n]$ exactly the shifted calculation holds: $F(B[n])=E[n]$, the only potentially nonzero degree of the unit is $q=-n$, and its map there is the same endomorphism identification. The cohomology criterion shows that $\eta_{B[n]}$ is invertible for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, proof; degree-zero endomorphism case, using its compactness argument only in D_QCoh.

proof.text: Apply the shift-saturated isomorphism-locus lemma to $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to GF$. Both functors are exact and preserve coproducts by the preceding steps. Its predicate $Q(M)$, invertibility of $\eta$ on every shift of $M$, is closed under isomorphisms, triangles and coproducts, and contains $B$. The compact-generator construction applied to the singleton family $\{B\}$ writes every $M$ as a telescope of stages starting with a sum of shifts of $B$ and obtained by triangles with sums of such shifts. Induction puts every stage in $Q$; the telescope triangle and coproduct closure then put $M$ in $Q$. Hence every $\eta_M$ is invertible, and naturality makes their inverses a natural inverse to $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 09LZ, lemma-fully-faithful-in-compact-case, proof; degree-zero endomorphism case, using its compactness argument only in D_QCoh.

proof.text: For $M,N\in\mathcal C$, the composite bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(FM,FN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,GFN)\xrightarrow{\eta_N^{-1}\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,N)$ is inverse to $f\mapsto Ff$: its value on $Ff$ is $\eta_N^{-1}GF(f)\eta_M=f$ by naturality. Bijectivity proves full faithfulness. The construction uses generation only by $B$ on the source, as required.

That last step uses lem-sc-shift-saturated-iso-locus and lem-pc-compact-generators-build-objects with the singleton {B}. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to live, the item is still unsplit live, there is no repair note and no new nodes, and proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Cited statements checked: the module direct-sum and homology-coproduct nodes are bound to [Ring R], so applying them to B^op is legitimate for noncommutative End(E). Compactness is used only against D_QCoh objects (step 4), consistent with the item hypothesis and the parent tilting node's use of it. Step 2 is the elementary B[0] Hom/cohomology calculation via the Mathlib K-projective leaf. Step 5: H^0(eta_B) is End(E)->End_D(E), which follows from F=V_E on the projective B; it is bijective by the single-functor leaf, and the adjunction's exactness handles the shifts. Edge cases checked: E=0, E=O_X affine, matrix rings. Duplicate search (09LZ/0BQU, fully faithful+compact) found only the parent chain. All five tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA citations.
